⚠️ Problem: Learner stresses suffix '-ment' in 'government'.
💡 Solution: Tap primary stress on GOV-ernment and whisper -ment.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Core Suffix Pronunciations (-tion, -sion, -ly, -ness, -ment)
1. Definition: Common derivative suffixes are unstressed and contain reduced schwa /ə/ or short /i/ vowels.
2. Rule: -tion = /ʃən/ (nation); -sion after vowel = /ʒən/ (vision); -sion after consonant = /ʃən/ (tension); -ly = /li/; -ness = /nəs/; -ment = /mənt/; -ful = /fəl/; -less = /ləs/.
3. Why? English rhythm reduces unstressed suffixes to schwa.
4. How to recognize? Identify common derivative endings.
5. Common examples: nation /ˈneɪʃən/, action, vision /ˈvɪʒən/, tension /ˈtɛnʃən/, quickly, kindness, moment, careful, homeless
6. Counter-examples: Full words ending in -ment (cement /sɪˈmɛnt/ = stressed full vowel).
7. Exceptions: suggestion /səˈdʒɛstʃən/ (-tion pronounced /tʃən/ after t).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing -tion as *ti-on or -ful as *full with long vowel.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: -tion = /ʃən/! -sion after vowel = /ʒən/! Reduce suffix vowels to schwa!
10. Key vocabulary: suffix, vowel reduction, schwa, palatal suffix, stressless ending
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 📉 Low pitch arrow over reduced suffix syllables.
14. Key Takeaway: -tion = /ʃən/, -sion = /ʒən/ or /ʃən/. Suffixes are weak!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How is '-tion' pronounced in 'nation'? (/ʃən/ with schwa)
CCQ 2: What is the difference in sound between '-sion' in 'vision' and 'tension'? (vision = voiced /ʒən/ after vowel; tension = voiceless /ʃən/ after consonant)
CCQ 3: Should suffix vowels like '-ful' in 'careful' be stressed or reduced? (Reduced to schwa /fəl/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
